clue.text: Piece of information obtained from US lawyer by corporation

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, and a paunch is a tum

explanation.surface: A fact gleaned from an American attorney working for a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is the old humorous word for a big belly, a TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or item of data, the singular of data.

clue.text: Take too long to capture old soldier

indicators.note: to capture means the phrase takes the letter for old inside it

parts.note: to drag on is to take too long

explanation.surface: Being slow to seize an aged veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Drum along with mildly vacuous rock opera

parts.note: a tom, or tom-tom, is a drum

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so mildly loses all its inner letters leaving the outside pair

explanation.surface: A drummer joins in a rather empty-headed rock opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is The Who's 1969 rock opera about a deaf, dumb and blind pinball player.

clue.text: NY district man finds hot area — time to catch some rays!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
catching rays of sunshine gives you a tan

explanation.surface: A New Yorker finds a hot spot and takes time off to sunbathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is one of the five boroughs of New York City.

clue.text: Computer programs tanks to surround castle

indicators.note: to surround means the tanks go round the castle's letter

parts.note: bowsers are tanker vehicles carrying fuel or water
R is the chess notation for a rook, also called a castle

explanation.surface: Military tanks encircling a castle, dressed up as computing jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowser is a mobile tank for fuel or water; R stands for rook, the chess piece also called a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Web browsers such as Firefox or Chrome are software applications for viewing pages.

clue.text: Supported leaving Europe, won unexpectedly — step away from the brink

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for Europe departs from the word

parts.note: backed means supported

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters of won land in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A political crisis: leaving Europe, an unlikely victory, and a retreat from disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: BACKED without E gives BACKD; WON rearranged gives OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is to withdraw from a confrontational position, retreating before things escalate.

clue.text: Characters from 16 learned way of working backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a sage is a wise, learned person
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: Letters from an ancient Greek playwright, studied by a scholar working in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is AESCHYLUS, who wrote in Greek, so his characters are Greek letters. SAGE then MO, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so omegas are characters a Greek writer would use.

clue.text: Material to exploit after initial downsizing

indicators.note: downsizing the initial means a clothing size goes down: medium at the front becomes small

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it

explanation.surface: A cloth exploited after early cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: On clothing labels M is medium and S small, so downsizing the first letter swaps M for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is a fine fabric spun by silkworms.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's artist companion describing limits of outdoor school

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so the artist's letters go round the rest

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: limits of means the first and last letters of outdoor

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's painter friend sketches the edge of an open-air school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its old geometric sense of drawing a line round something. The 's on Psychiatrist stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Rorschach was the Swiss psychiatrist who devised the inkblot test.

clue.text: Two bands taken up river

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: Yes and REM are two rock bands

explanation.surface: Two groups pick up the river as a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: YES then REM, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mersey is the English river that flows to the sea at Liverpool.

clue.text: Local man acquires sports calendar

indicators.note: sports in the sense of wears or displays, so the words show off the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A local man buys himself a calendar of sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' looks like part of 'sports calendar', but it is the signal: the phrase displays the answer across 'locAL MAN ACquires'.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly publication arranged by dates, like Wisden for cricket.

clue.text: Expand integral needing brackets put back

indicators.note: put back means the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
brackets as a verb: the words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A maths instruction to expand an integral whose brackets need restoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'integral' and 'brackets' suggest algebra; in fact 'integrAL NEEDing' holds EGRALNE, and reading that backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to make it bigger, which is what expanding does.

clue.text: Once-great king of magical city rumoured to be returning after many struggles

parts.note: Oz is the magical land and Emerald City of the Wizard of Oz

indicators.note: the word many struggles, writhing into a new order
returning means the word is read from the end backwards

parts.note: something rumoured is said

explanation.surface: A fallen monarch of an enchanted city, gossip says, comes back after many battles.
explanation.walkthrough: MANY rearranged gives YMAN; SAID read backwards gives DIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozymandias is the Greek name of the pharaoh Ramesses II, whose ruined statue Shelley's sonnet describes.

clue.text: Pros and cons explained succinctly at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A brief summary of the arguments for and against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pros and cons' reads as one phrase, but 'Pros' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are experts or top performers, as professionals are.

clue.text: One who prefers late hours with long parties

indicators.note: parties as a verb, like divides or splits, so the letters are parted and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps late hours and goes to lengthy parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' looks like a noun for the late nights, but it is a verb telling you to break up WITH LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A night owl is a person who stays up and is most active late in the evening.

clue.text: State university team performing in swimming contest

indicators.note: in means the university and team letters go inside the contest

parts.note: a gala is a swimming competition in British usage

indicators.note: performing means the team's letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A college squad competing at a swimming event.
explanation.walkthrough: A swimming gala is the usual British name for a competitive swimming meet. TEAM rearranged gives ATEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a Central American country, and a state means a nation.

clue.text: Singer is allowed to alter opening lines

parts.note: if you are allowed to, you can

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of alter

parts.note: RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A vocalist is permitted to change the first lines of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a songbird, and singer is a crossword name for any songbird.

clue.text: I shunned such easily translated ancient Greek

indicators.note: shunned means the I is avoided, left out of the letters
translated means the letters of such easily are converted into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone avoided an ancient Greek text that was so easily translated.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SUCH EASILY, drop the I, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus was the Athenian tragedian, the earliest of the great Greek playwrights.

clue.text: Entertainer to visit princess briefly

parts.note: to come is to visit

indicators.note: briefly means the princess's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Diana, the Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A performer calling briefly on a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a performer who makes audiences laugh.

clue.text: Smart to corner right niche

indicators.note: to corner means the shrewd word traps the letter for right inside it

parts.note: canny means shrewd or smart

explanation.surface: A clever way to box in the right recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small narrow opening or recess, as in nooks and crannies.

clue.text: Opt for designer snakeskin

parts.note: Jimmy Choo is a shoe designer
the skin of snake, its outer letters

explanation.surface: Choosing snakeskin from a fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to select or opt for something.

clue.text: Exotic broths featuring toppings of sour cream

definitions.text: Exotic broths featuring toppings of sour cream

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging
toppings of takes the top, first letter of sour and of cream

explanation.surface: Foreign soups served with a dollop of sour cream on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: BROTHS plus S and C rearranged gives the soups, which are themselves topped with sour cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht is an Eastern European beetroot soup traditionally served with sour cream.

clue.text: It's scary to behave like Ofsted, dropping in on Bible study

indicators.note: dropping means the word in falls out

parts.note: Ofsted is the English schools inspectorate, so behaving like it is to inspect
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: School inspectors dropping in on a scripture lesson is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in on' reads as paying a visit, but it splits into a removal signal, the removed word and a placing word. Ofsted is the body that inspects English schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost, something frightening.

clue.text: Game is protected by trademark law

indicators.note: protected by means the game and is are kept inside the trademark letters

parts.note: TM is the trademark sign
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A sport protected by trademark law.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a self-evident statement, an accepted principle stated as if a rule.

clue.text: Public duck enclosure

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, which looks like O
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A duck pond's fenced area open to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is accessible to everyone, not restricted or private.

clue.text: Some work around opera company securing hotel before function for conservatory

indicators.note: around means the unit is turned round

parts.note: an erg is a unit of work in physics

indicators.note: securing means the opera company holds the hotel letter inside it

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
a use is a function or purpose

explanation.surface: Some renovation at an opera house, including a hotel wing, for a conservatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some work' looks like a vague phrase, but it is the physics unit of work. English National Opera is the London company usually clued as 'opera company'.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse is a glass building for growing plants, much like a conservatory.

clue.text: Complaint about displacing holy man from Northern Ireland

indicators.note: displacing means one piece pushes the other out of the word and takes its place

parts.note: Ulster is a common name for Northern Ireland
ST is short for saint
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A grievance about a priest being forced out of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is a sore, and complaint is a word for a medical ailment.

clue.text: Record no end of dance music

indicators.note: no end of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: disco is a style of dance music

explanation.surface: An endless supply of dance tracks on vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it cuts the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or CD.

clue.text: Language inverting rules about greeting with personal pronoun

indicators.note: about means the turned word wraps round the greeting
inverting means the word for rules is turned back to front

parts.note: laws are rules
hi is a greeting
I is the first-person personal pronoun

explanation.surface: A language that flips grammar rules about how to greet someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu tongue widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: Forbidden to provoke in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out or provoke a response

explanation.surface: Something banned for being said to stir people up.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means not allowed by law or custom, i.e. prohibited.

clue.text: Revolutionary peasant can have military leaders' opponents as guards

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of can, have and military

parts.note: in bridge, East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N

explanation.surface: A rebel peasant can take on army officers' enemies as his bodyguards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'military leaders' looks like generals, but 'leaders' picks the first letters of 'can have military'. E and N are bridge partners' opponents, East and North.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchmen are people employed to keep watch and protect property, like guards.

clue.text: Southern Canadian rock group on downward trajectory

parts.note: the Cree are an indigenous people of Canada

explanation.surface: A rock band from southern Canada whose career is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock group' suggests a band, but here it is a mass of stones sliding down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is a mass of loose stones on a mountainside that tends to slide downhill.
